question.problem:
Given that $X$ is a continuous random variable with the following probability density function, compute $\text{E}[2e-(e-1)X].$

$$
f(x)=\frac{e}{e{x}^{2}-{x}^{2}},\,1<x<e
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, we simplify using the properties of expected value:

$$
\text{E}[2e-(e-1)X]=2e-(e-1)\text{E}[X]
$$

For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the expected value using the following formula:

$$
\text{E}[X]={\int }_{S}x\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

So, we calculate the expected value of $X$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\int }_{S}x\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{e}x\cdot \frac{e}{e{x}^{2}-{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{e}{ex-x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{e}{e-1}{\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{e}{e-1}\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡x|}_{1}^{e} \\  & =\frac{e}{e-1}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[2e-(e-1)X] & =2e-(e-1)\text{E}[X] \\  & =2e-(e-1)\cdot \frac{e}{e-1} \\  & =2e-e \\  & =e.\end{aligned}
$$
